lessons.title: Early Cycle Leaders: Banks, Autos, Real Estate, and Consumer Discretionary

body.text: Early cycle leaders share one trait: their earnings were hit hardest by the downturn, and they are the first to benefit when rates fall and deferred spending returns. The market buys that rebound long before it shows up in the data.

children.text: Lesson 3.1 laid out the rotation clock and the mechanics behind it. This lesson zooms into the first position on the clock: the sectors that have historically led as an economy moves from contraction into recovery. For India, that means banks and financials, autos, real estate, and consumer discretionary businesses. For each one, you will learn why it tends to lead, which Indian data to track, and the signals that its leadership is running out.
What Makes a Sector an Early Cycle Leader?

body.caption: The early cycle group at a glance

children.text: Three forces run through all four sectors: sensitivity to interest rates, pent-up demand for purchases that can be postponed, and operating leverage that turns a modest revenue recovery into a sharp profit rebound.
Banks and Financials

markDefs.definition: The provisions a bank sets aside for expected loan losses during a period, usually expressed as a percentage of average loans. High credit costs in a downturn crush bank profits; falling credit costs in a recovery lift them sharply.

children.text: Banks lead early in a recovery for a reason many investors miss. It is not mainly about loan growth, which comes later. It is about
credit cost
. In a downturn, provisions for bad loans eat most of a bank's profit. When bad loans peak and start falling, those provisions drop, and profits can multiply even if loan growth is still modest.

body.caption: A simplified bank return on assets tree, with every item expressed as a percentage of average assets

body.title: Watch Credit Costs Drive Profits
body.prompt: A bank has a net interest margin of 3.2%, other income of 1.0%, operating costs of 2.0%, and a tax rate of 25%, all relative to assets. In the downturn its credit cost was 1.6%, giving an RoA of 0.45%. In the recovery, credit cost falls to 0.6% and nothing else changes. What is the new RoA, in percent?
body.explanation: Pre-tax return rises from 3.2 + 1.0 minus 2.0 minus 1.6 = 0.6% to 3.2 + 1.0 minus 2.0 minus 0.6 = 1.6%. After 25% tax, RoA goes from 0.45% to 1.20%, more than two and a half times higher, with no change in margins or loan growth. This is why bank stocks can rally hard at the point when the headlines are still about bad loans: the market is pricing the fall in credit costs ahead.

body.text: Remember the margin trap from Lesson 2.3. When the RBI cuts rates, banks with mostly repo-linked loans see loan yields fall faster than deposit costs, which can squeeze margins in the early quarters of an easing cycle. Early cycle bank leadership usually depends on credit costs falling and credit growth recovering by more than margins compress. Lenders exposed to unsecured consumer credit carry an extra risk, as the RBI's November 2023 risk weight increase showed.

children.text: Autos

A car or motorcycle is the classic deferrable purchase. When jobs feel insecure or EMIs look expensive, households postpone it; when confidence returns and loan rates fall, pent-up demand floods back. Carmakers and component suppliers also have large fixed costs in plants and dealer networks, so volume recovery drops straight to profit.

body.title: India passenger vehicle domestic wholesales (lakh units)

children.text: Domestic passenger vehicle wholesales fell to 27.1 lakh units in FY21, the Covid year, then rose for five straight years to a record 46.4 lakh units in FY26, an increase of about 71% from the low. The biggest jump came in FY23, as semiconductor shortages eased and pent-up demand was released.

body.label: GST 2.0 and the auto cycle
body.value: Small cars: 28% GST cut to 18% from 22 September 2025
body.context: Combined with RBI rate cuts and income tax relief, it helped the October 2025 festive season set a record for retail vehicle sales, and SIAM credited it with supporting record FY26 passenger vehicle sales.

children.text: Two-wheelers tell a more cautious story. Domestic two-wheeler sales peaked at about 21 million units in FY19, and even after growing 9.1% in FY25 they reached only 19.6 million. Two-wheelers are the better gauge of rural and lower-income demand, and their slower recovery is a reminder that an early cycle rebound is rarely even across income groups.

body.text: Within autos, match the segment to the part of the cycle. Two-wheelers and tractors reflect rural incomes and monsoons. Entry-level cars reflect first-time buyers and affordability. SUVs and premium cars reflect urban, higher-income confidence. Commercial vehicles, especially trucks, reflect freight and capex, and tend to recover later, alongside the investment cycle.

children.text: Real Estate

Housing combines the most rate sensitive purchase most households ever make with a highly leveraged, fixed-cost industry. When home loan rates fall and incomes feel secure, sales can surge; when rates rise or confidence cracks, buyers step back fast.

body.caption: How loan rates change affordability: ₹50 lakh home loan over 20 years

body.title: Feel the EMI Swing
body.prompt: Using the table, the EMI on a ₹50 lakh, 20-year loan is ₹38,018 at 6.75% and ₹45,793 at 9.25%. By roughly what percentage does the EMI rise when the loan rate goes from 6.75% to 9.25%? Round to the nearest whole number.
body.explanation: ₹45,793 divided by ₹38,018 is about 1.205, an increase of about 20.5%. A 2.5 percentage point rise in loan rates, similar to the 250 bps RBI hiking cycle of 2022 to 2023 passing through to repo-linked home loans, raises the monthly payment on the same house by about a fifth. Put the other way, falling rates let a buyer afford a noticeably bigger loan on the same income, which is why real estate reacts early to an easing cycle.

body.title: Housing sales in India's top 7 cities (lakh units, ANAROCK)

children.text: The chart shows a full real estate cycle. Sales halved to 1.38 lakh units in 2020, recovered to 2.37 lakh in 2021, and then rose to a record 4.77 lakh in 2023, up about 246% from the Covid low. Notice that 2022 and 2023 were strong years even though the RBI was hiking: after nearly a decade of flat prices and falling inventory, housing had its own cycle of pent-up demand and improving affordability relative to incomes. Volumes then eased, and in 2025 sales fell about 14% to 3.96 lakh units, even as the total value of homes sold rose about 6%, as the mix shifted towards more expensive homes.

body.text: Real estate cycles are longer and lumpier than the business cycle. Interest rates matter, but so do unsold inventory, price levels relative to incomes, regulation, and developer balance sheets. That is why real estate can keep rising through a hiking cycle, as in 2022 to 2023, or lag well into a recovery. Treat interest rates as necessary but not sufficient.

children.text: Consumer Discretionary

Consumer discretionary covers what people buy when they feel good about the future: consumer durables such as air conditioners and washing machines, apparel and retail, hotels and travel, restaurants, and entertainment. After a downturn these businesses benefit from pent-up demand and from operating leverage, since stores, hotels, and factories carry high fixed costs.
Post-Covid, travel and hospitality saw a strong "revenge travel" rebound once restrictions lifted, a textbook early cycle move off a collapsed base.
Policy can add fuel. In FY26, lower GST rates from September 2025 and personal income tax relief announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 both put more money in consumers' pockets.
Watch for a split recovery. Premium brands and urban spending often recover earlier and faster than mass-market and rural spending, so the same sector can contain very different trends.
When Early Cycle Leadership Fades

body.title: Early Cycle Signals: Entry vs Exit

columns.label: Signals that favour early cycle sectors

Gross NPAs and bank credit costs peaking and starting to fall
Monthly auto and housing sales improving from depressed levels
Scorecard moving from contraction into recovery

columns.label: Signals that leadership is maturing
points: RBI on hold or turning towards tightening; bond yields rising
Credit costs at cyclical lows with little room left to fall
Sales growth slowing after a pent-up demand wave is spent
Regulators leaning against fast-growing loan segments

body.title: Go deeper: a monthly early cycle checklist using Indian data

children.text: First days of each month: company auto sales, then FADA retail registrations to confirm real demand.
RBI sectoral credit data: growth in housing loans, vehicle loans, and credit to NBFCs.
Quarterly results: credit costs and gross NPA trends at large private and PSU banks.
Quarterly housing reports: sales, launches, and unsold inventory across the top cities.
RBI policy statements: stance, repo rate, and any regulatory moves on consumer lending.

content.title: Is This an Early Cycle Setup?
steps: The RBI has cut rates or signalled easing within the last two policy meetings
Bank credit costs have peaked and gross NPAs are falling
Auto retail sales have grown for at least three months on a year-on-year basis
Housing sales are improving from a clear low, not already at record highs
Early cycle sector valuations are below their own long-run averages

children.text: Practice

body.title: The Hidden Driver of Bank Profits
body.textWithBlank: In an early recovery, bank profits can jump even with modest loan growth, mainly because ___ fall as bad loans peak and provisions shrink.
body.explanation: Falling credit costs, the provisions set aside for loan losses, are often the single biggest driver of bank earnings recovery early in a cycle. Loan growth and margins matter more later.

body.title: Real Estate and Rates
body.question: Housing sales in India's top 7 cities rose to a record in 2023 even though the RBI raised the repo rate by 250 bps between May 2022 and February 2023. What is the best explanation?
options: Interest rates have no effect on housing demand
Housing has its own cycle of inventory, prices, and affordability; after years of flat prices and falling inventory, pent-up demand outweighed higher loan rates
The RBI hikes did not pass through to home loan rates at all
Housing sales data is unreliable and should be ignored
body.explanation: Higher rates did make home loans more expensive, especially for repo-linked loans. But the housing market came out of a long stagnant phase with limited new supply, stable prices relative to rising incomes, and pent-up demand after Covid. Those forces outweighed the rate increase for a time. It is a reminder that interest rates are one driver of real estate, not the only one.

body.title: Spot the Early Cycle Opportunity
body.scenario: Imagine the economy is emerging from a sharp slowdown. The RBI has cut the repo rate by 100 bps over six months and moved to an accommodative stance. Large banks report that gross NPAs have peaked and slippages are falling, but loan growth is still only 9%. Monthly car wholesales are up 12% year on year, while FADA retail registrations are up 4%. Housing sales for the last quarter are 20% below their previous peak but rising. Bank and auto indices have already risen 25% from their lows, while FMCG has been flat.
body.prompt: Which early cycle sectors look best supported by the data, what would you check before concluding the rally has further to go, and what is the main risk in each?
body.modelAnswer: Banks look best supported: falling slippages point to lower credit costs, which drive profits even while loan growth is modest, and the RBI is easing. The main risk is margin compression if loans reprice down faster than deposits, and whether credit growth actually picks up. Autos are supported by rate cuts, but the gap between 12% wholesale growth and 4% retail growth suggests dealer inventory is building, so check FADA inventory commentary and whether retail catches up before assuming demand is strong. Real estate has room to recover since sales are still 20% below the peak, but check unsold inventory and pricing before concluding affordability has improved enough. Across all three, a 25% rally means some recovery is already priced in, so compare valuations with long-run averages and watch whether earnings estimates are being revised up. This is an analysis of evidence, not a recommendation to buy any of these sectors.

body.text: This lesson is educational. Sector patterns described are historical tendencies, not predictions, and the examples use data that will be revised or superseded. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy, sell, or overweight any sector, stock, index, or fund.

points: Early cycle leaders, banks, autos, real estate, and consumer discretionary, share rate sensitivity, pent-up demand for deferrable purchases, and high operating leverage
Bank earnings in a recovery are driven first by falling credit costs: in the example, cutting credit cost from 1.6% to 0.6% lifted RoA from 0.45% to 1.2%
Indian bank gross NPAs fell from above 11% in March 2018 to 2.3% in March 2025, with 2024-25 RoA of 1.4% and RoE of 13.5%
Passenger vehicle wholesales rose from 27.1 lakh units in FY21 to a record 46.4 lakh in FY26, helped by pent-up demand, rate cuts, and GST 2.0; two-wheelers remain below their FY19 peak
A rise in home loan rates from 6.75% to 9.25% lifts the EMI on a ₹50 lakh, 20-year loan by about 20%
Top 7 city housing sales went from 1.38 lakh units in 2020 to a record 4.77 lakh in 2023, then eased to 3.96 lakh in 2025, showing real estate has its own, longer cycle
Early cycle leadership fades as rates stop falling, credit costs bottom out, pent-up demand is spent, and valuations price in peak earnings
